column1: # Which kernels exist, what they need, and how to build them.
# One source of truth for every benchmark runner, so the binary list is not
# duplicated across perf_check.sh, baseline.sh and distributed.sh.
# benchmarks/tools/select_kernels.py reads this and applies the filtering.
#   path          <kernel-dir>/<binary-name> as produced by the dir's Makefile
#   min_dev       fewest GPUs the binary will run on
#   max_dev       most GPUs it will use; 0 means no upper bound, and a value
#                 equal to min_dev means it accepts that count and no other
#   tier          fast  = single-GPU, cheap and quiet; the PR gate default
#                 multi = needs more than one GPU
#   make_target   target that produces it, as `make -C kernels/<dir> <target>`
# A binary runs when min_dev <= visible GPUs. When max_dev == min_dev it also
# refuses any other count, because its NUM_DEVICES is compiled in with no
# environment override. Single-GPU kernels use max_dev 0: they run on a 12-tile
# host perfectly well, they just use one device.
# Covers the matrix, reduction and elementwise paths without the latency
# probes or the oneMKL dependency that make the rest flaky to build.
# decode links oneMKL for its GEMV fallback; needs MKLROOT on CPATH.
# -- multi GPU, scales with the device count ------------------------------
# These three read SK_NUM_DEVICES, so they run on any count from 2 up.
# These three take min(visible, NUM_DEVICES_MAX), so they adapt on their own.
# NUM_DEVICES is compiled in with no environment override, so these refuse to
# run on anything but the exact count. benchmarks/suites/distributed.sh drives
# them, since they also need an externally supplied ZE_AFFINITY_MASK.
